Graph Theory, Part Two

本讲内容 游走, 路径与可达性 补图 鸽巢原理 鸽巢原理的派对把戏 推广的鸽巢原理 应用: 朋友与陌生人

本讲内容
Outline for Today

Slide 2–4

Outline for Today

  • Walks, Paths, and Reachability
    • Walking around a graph.
  • Graph Complements
    • Flipping what's in a graph.
  • The Pigeonhole Principle
    • Everyone finding a place.

Recap from Last Time — Graphs and Digraphs

  • A graph is a pair G=(V,E) of a set of nodes V and set of edges E.
  • Nodes can be anything.
  • Edges are unordered pairs (i.e., sets with cardinality 2) of nodes. If {u,v}∈E, then there's an edge from u to v.

这一讲在图上「走路」: 定义游走、路径、闭游走、圈、可达、连通和连通分量; 然后讲补图, 证明 G 和补图至少一个连通; 最后讲鸽巢原理及其推广, 用它证明「派对上总有两人朋友数相同」和六人派对定理. 重点是这几个定义的细微区别和鸽巢原理的用法.

游走, 路径与可达性
Walks, Paths, and Reachability

Slide 7–8

(图: 单词图 CAN、MAN、RAN、MAT、CAT、SAT、RAT.)

Two nodes are called adjacent if there is an edge between them.

Using our Formalisms

  • Let G=(V,E) be a graph.
  • Intuitively, two nodes are adjacent if they're linked by an edge.
  • Formally speaking, we say that two nodes u,v∈V are adjacent if we have {u,v}∈E.

两个节点之间有边, 就叫它们 adjacent 相邻. 正式定义: u,v∈V 相邻当且仅当 {u,v}∈E. 例如单词图里 CAT 和 SAT 相邻, CAT 和 RAN 不相邻.

Slide 9–19

(图: 美国西部州际公路地图, 抽象成以城市为节点的图.)

From SF To Sea: SF, Sac, Port, Sea
SF, Sac, SLC, Port, Sea
SF, Sac, LA, Phoe, Flag, Bar, LV, Mon, SLC, But, Sea

A walk in a graph G=(V,E) is a sequence of one or more nodes v1​,v2​,v3​,…,vn​ such that any two consecutive nodes in the sequence are adjacent.

The length of the walk v1​,…,vn​ is n−1.

(This walk has length 10, but visits 11 cities.)

把美国西部的城市 (Sea 西雅图、Port 波特兰、SF 旧金山、Sac 萨克拉门托、SLC 盐湖城、But 比尤特、Mon 蒙大拿方向、LV 拉斯维加斯、Bar 巴斯托、Flag 弗拉格斯塔夫、LA、Phoe 凤凰城、SD 圣迭戈、Nog 诺加莱斯) 和公路画成图. 从 SF 到 Sea 有很多走法, 课件列了三种.

walk 游走: 一个或多个节点组成的序列, 相邻两项必须相邻. 游走的 length 长度是边的条数, 即节点数减 1. 第三种走法经过 11 个城市, 长度是 10.

Slide 20

Question: Is a “staycation” a valid walk? In other words, can a walk be just “SF”?

可以. 定义要求「一个或多个节点」, 只有 SF 一个节点的序列满足条件 (没有相邻的两项要检查), 是长度为 0 的游走. 所以每个节点都能「走到」自己.

Slide 21–24

From/To Sea: Sea, But, SLC, Port, Sea

From/To Sac: Sac, Port, Sea, But, SLC, Mon, LV, Bar, LA, Sac

A closed walk in a graph is a walk from a node back to itself. (By convention, a closed walk cannot have length zero.)

(No “staycation” in closed walks, because of this rule.)

closed walk 闭游走: 起点和终点是同一个节点的游走. 按约定长度不能为 0, 所以「原地不动」不算闭游走. 例子 Sac → … → Sac 共 10 项, 长度 9, 中间经过 9 个不同城市.

Slide 25–37

SF, Sac, LA, Phoe, Flag, Bar, LA

A path in a graph is walk that does not repeat any nodes.

(A walk, not a path.)

Sac, SLC, Port, Sac, SLC, Port, Sac

(This walk has length six.)

path 路径: 不重复经过任何节点的游走. SF, Sac, LA, Phoe, Flag, Bar, LA 是游走 (每步都沿着边), 但 LA 出现了两次, 所以不是路径. 绕三角形 Sac–SLC–Port 两圈的序列有 7 项, 长度 6.

Slide 38–49

A cycle in a graph is a closed walk that does not repeat any nodes or edges except the first/last node.

(A closed walk, not a cycle.)

cycle 圈: 除了首尾是同一个节点外, 不重复任何节点或边的闭游走. 绕三角形一圈 Sac, SLC, Port, Sac 是圈; 绕两圈就重复了节点和边, 只是闭游走.

为什么还要求不重复边? 否则 A, B, A 这种「走过去再原路返回」就成了长度 2 的圈. 不重复边的要求排除了它, 所以圈至少有 3 条边 (见下文 Fun Facts).

Slide 50

What is the length of the longest walk in this graph? Path? Closed walk? Cycle?

答案:

  • 游走和闭游走: 没有最长, 可以沿着一条边来回走任意多次, 长度无上限.
  • 路径: 最长是 13. 按原图连边枚举, 例如 But, Sea, Port, SLC, Mon, LV, Bar, Flag, Phoe, Nog, SD, LA, Sac, SF, 经过全部 14 个城市.
  • 圈: 最长是 13, 例如 Sea, Port, Sac, LA, SD, Nog, Phoe, Flag, Bar, LV, Mon, SLC, But, Sea. SF 只连着 Sac, 不可能在圈里, 所以圈最多包含其余 13 个城市.

路径和圈的长度是用 Python 按原图的 18 条边穷举得到的.

Slide 54–61

A node v is reachable from a node u if there is a path from u to v.

(Barstow isn't reachable from SF after these road closures.)

A graph G is called connected if all pairs of distinct nodes in G are reachable.

(This graph is not connected.)

A connected component (or CC) of G is a maximal set of mutually reachable nodes.

三个相关定义:

  • reachable 可达: 存在一条从 u 到 v 的路径.
  • connected 连通: 任意两个不同的节点都互相可达. 删掉几条公路后, 从 SF 到不了 Barstow, 图就不连通了.
  • connected component 连通分量 (CC): 一组互相可达的节点, 而且是「极大的」, 不能再加入任何节点而保持互相可达. 原图里北边和南边各是一个连通分量.

易错: 「极大」(maximal) 不是「最大」(maximum). 极大指不能再扩展; 一个图可以有多个连通分量, 每个都是极大的, 大小可以不同.

Slide 62

Fun Facts

  • Here's a collection of useful facts about graphs that you can take as a given.
    • Theorem: If G=(V,E) is a graph and u,v∈V, then there is a path from u to v if and only if there's a walk from u to v.
    • Theorem: If G is a graph and C is a cycle in G, then C's length is at least three and C contains at least three nodes.
    • Theorem: If G=(V,E) is a graph, then every node in V belongs to exactly one connected component of G.
    • Theorem: If G=(V,E) is a graph, then G is connected if and only if G has exactly one connected component.
  • Looking for more practice working with formal definitions? Prove these results!

可以直接引用的四个事实:

  1. u 到 v 有路径当且仅当有游走. 路径本身就是游走; 反过来, 游走中如果重复了节点, 就把两次出现之间的部分剪掉, 直到不重复.
  2. 圈的长度至少 3, 至少含 3 个节点. 长度 1 需要自环, 长度 2 需要重复边, 都被排除.
  3. 每个节点恰好属于一个连通分量: 「互相可达」把节点分成互不相交的块.
  4. 图连通当且仅当它恰好有一个连通分量.

补图
Graph Complements

Slide 64

Let G=(V,E) be an undirected graph. The complement of G is the graph Gc=(V,Ec), where

Ec={{u,v}∣u∈V,v∈V,u=v, and {u,v}∈/E}

complement 补图 Gc: 节点相同, 边恰好「翻转」: 原来不相邻的两个不同节点在补图里相邻, 原来相邻的在补图里不相邻. 定义里的 u=v 保证补图也没有自环. 把 G 和 Gc 的边合在一起, 正好是所有节点对, 即完全图.

Slide 65–67

Theorem: For any graph G=(V,E), at least one of G and Gc is connected.

Proving a Disjunction

  • We need to prove the statement G is connected ∨ Gc is connected.
  • Here's a neat observation.
    • If G is connected, we're done.
    • Otherwise, G isn't connected, and we have to prove that Gc is connected.
  • We will therefore prove

    For any graph G=(V,E), if G is not connected, then Gc is connected.

定理: 任意图 G 和它的补图至少有一个是连通的. 要证的是一个「或」. 按技巧表, 证 A∨B 就证 ¬A→B: 如果 G 连通, 已经成立; 否则假设 G 不连通, 证明 Gc 连通.

Slide 68–73

Pick arbitrary nodes u and v from different connected components. Is it possible that {u,v}∈E? Why or why not?

Any two nodes in G in different CC's of G become adjacent in Gc.

Any two nodes in G in the same CC can be “bridged” in Gc through a node in a different CC of G.

课堂提问: 来自不同连通分量的 u、v 之间不可能有边. 如果有边 {u, v}, u 到 v 就有路径, 它们就在同一个分量里了.

由此得到证明思路 (读图):

  • u、v 在 G 的不同分量里: 它们在 G 中不相邻, 所以在 Gc 中直接相邻.
  • u、v 在 G 的同一分量里: G 不连通, 所以至少还有另一个分量, 从中任取一个节点 z. z 和 u、z 和 v 都在不同分量, 所以在补图中都相邻, 走 u, z, v 即可. z 起了「桥」的作用.
Slide 74–87

Theorem: If G=(V,E) is a graph, then at least one of G and Gc is connected.

Proof: Let G=(V,E) be an arbitrary graph and assume G is not connected. We need to show that Gc=(V,Ec) is connected. To do so, consider any two distinct nodes u,v∈V. We need to show that there is a path from u to v in Gc. We consider two cases:

Case 1: u and v are in different connected components of G. This means that {u,v}∈/E, since otherwise the path u,v would make u reachable from v and they'd be in the same connected component of G. Therefore, we see that {u,v}∈Ec, and so there is a path (namely, u,v) from u to v in Gc.

Case 2: u and v are in the same connected component of G. Since G is not connected, there are at least two connected components of G. Pick any node z that belongs to a different connected component of G than u and v. Then by the reasoning from Case 1 we know that {u,z}∈Ec and {z,v}∈Ec. This gives a path u,z,v in Gc from u to v.

In either case, we find a path from u to v in Gc, as required. ■

正式证明按上面的思路分两种情况. 「连通」的定义是 ∀u,v (不同节点) 可达, 所以任取 u ≠ v; 然后对 u、v 是否在同一分量分情况 (假设里的 ∨: 两个节点要么在同一分量, 要么不在).

情况 2 里还要说明 u, z, v 确实是路径: z 与 u、v 在不同分量, 所以 z 不等于 u 或 v, 三个节点各不相同.

幻灯片前后不一致: Slide 83–85 的情况 2 一度写成 “Since G is not connected, there is at least one node that is not connected to u or v—pick one such node and call it z.”, Slide 87 起改成上面的写法. 前一种说法含糊 (「不连到 u 或 v」可以理解成只和其中一个不可达), 改后的「属于与 u、v 不同的连通分量」才准确.

鸽巢原理
The Pigeonhole Principle

Slide 89–94

Theorem (The Pigeonhole Principle): If m objects are distributed into n bins and m>n, then at least one bin will contain at least two objects.

(插图: m = 4 只鸽子, n = 3 个鸽巢, 有一个巢里挤了两只. 作者 Amy Liu.)

Some Simple Applications

  • Any group of 367 people must have a pair of people that share a birthday.
    • 366 possible birthdays (pigeonholes).
    • 367 people (pigeons).
  • Two people in San Francisco have the exact same number of hairs on their head.
    • Maximum number of hairs ever found on a human head is no greater than 500,000.
    • There are over 800,000 people in San Francisco.

pigeonhole principle 鸽巢原理: 把 m 个物品放进 n 个盒子, 若 m > n, 则至少有一个盒子里有两个或更多物品. 例子:

  • 生日有 366 种 (算上 2 月 29 日), 367 个人里一定有两人同一天生日.
  • 人头上的头发不超过 50 万根, 头发数是 0 到 500 000 之间的整数, 最多 500 001 种; 旧金山有 80 多万人, 所以一定有两人头发根数相同.

鸽巢原理是存在性的: 它说明一定有某个盒子满足条件, 但不告诉你是哪一个.

Slide 95

Theorem (The Pigeonhole Principle): If m objects are distributed into n bins and m>n, then at least one bin will contain at least two objects.

Let A and B be finite sets (sets whose cardinalities are natural numbers) and assume ∣A∣>∣B∣. How many of the following statements are true?

  1. If f:A→B, then f is injective.
  2. If f:A→B, then f is not injective.
  3. If f:A→B, then f is surjective.
  4. If f:A→B, then f is not surjective.

只有 (2) 一定成立. 把 A 的元素当鸽子, B 的元素当巢, f 把每只鸽子放进一个巢. 鸽子比巢多, 所以必有两只鸽子在同一巢, 即两个不同输入有相同输出, f 不是单射. (1) 因此为假. (3)(4) 都不一定: 例如 A={1,2,3}, B={a,b}, 把 1、2 送到 a, 3 送到 b 是满射; 全送到 a 就不是满射.

Slide 97

Theorem: If m objects are distributed into n bins and m>n, then there must be some bin that contains at least two objects.

Proof: Suppose for the sake of contradiction that, for some m and n where m>n, there is a way to distribute m objects into n bins such that each bin contains at most one object.

Number the bins 1,2,3,…,n and let xi​ denote the number of objects in bin i. There are m objects in total, so we know that

m=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​.

Since each bin has at most one object in it, we know xi​≤1 for each i. This means that

m​amp;=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​amp;≤1+1+⋯+1(n times)amp;=n.​

This means that m≤n, contradicting that m>n. We've reached a contradiction, so our assumption must have been wrong. Therefore, if m objects are distributed into n bins with m>n, some bin must contain at least two objects. ■

证明用反证: 假设每个盒子至多一个物品. 设第 i 个盒子有 xi​ 个, 总数 m=∑xi​. 每个 xi​≤1, 所以 m≤n, 与 m>n 矛盾. 核心就是「每个都不超过 1, 加起来不超过 n」.

鸽巢原理的派对把戏
Pigeonhole Principle Party Tricks

Slide 102

Degrees

  • The degree of a node v in a graph is the number of nodes that v is adjacent to.
  • Theorem: Every graph with at least two nodes has at least two nodes with the same degree.
    • Equivalently: at any party with at least two people, there are at least two people with the same number of friends at the party.

(图: 一个七节点的图, 各节点旁标着度数 3, 2, 1, 3, 1, 0, 3.)

节点的 degree 度数是与它相邻的节点个数. 定理: 至少有两个节点的图里, 一定有两个节点度数相同. 换成派对的说法: 两人以上的派对上, 一定有两个人在场的朋友数相同. 例图里度数为 3 的节点有三个.

Slide 103–109

You've seen different edge possibilities for a graph with ∣V∣=6. How many different degrees is it possible for vertex A to have in any such graph?

With n nodes, there are n possible degrees (0,1,2,…,n−1)

Can both of these buckets be nonempty?

6 个节点时, A 最多和其余 5 个相邻, 度数可以是 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 共 6 种. 一般地 n 个节点有 n 种可能的度数, 正好和节点数一样多, 鸽巢原理还不能直接用.

关键观察: 度数为 0 和度数为 n − 1 的两个「盒子」不能同时有节点. 度数 n − 1 的节点和所有其他节点相邻, 包括那个度数为 0 的节点, 矛盾. 所以把这两个盒子合成一个, 只剩 n − 1 个盒子, 放 n 个节点, 鸽巢原理生效.

Slide 110

Theorem: In any graph with at least two nodes, there are at least two nodes of the same degree.

Proof 1: Let G be a graph with n≥2 nodes. There are n possible choices for the degrees of nodes in G, namely, 0,1,2,…, and n−1.

We claim that G cannot simultaneously have a node u of degree 0 and a node v of degree n−1: if there were such nodes, then node u would be adjacent to no other nodes and node v would be adjacent to all other nodes, including u. (Note that u and v must be different nodes, since v has degree at least 1 and u has degree 0.)

We therefore see that the possible options for degrees of nodes in G are either drawn from 0,1,…,n−2 or from 1,2,…,n−1. In either case, there are n nodes and n−1 possible degrees, so by the pigeonhole principle two nodes in G must have the same degree. ■

证明一: 先论证 0 和 n − 1 不能同时出现 (括号里还说明了 u、v 是不同的节点: n ≥ 2 时 n − 1 ≥ 1, 而 u 的度数是 0). 于是度数要么全在 0..n−2, 要么全在 1..n−1, 都只有 n − 1 种, n 个节点放进 n − 1 个盒子, 必有两个相同.

Slide 119

Proof 2: Assume for the sake of contradiction that there is a graph G with n≥2 nodes where no two nodes have the same degree. There are n possible choices for the degrees of nodes in G, namely 0,1,2,…,n−1, so this means that G must have exactly one node of each degree. However, this means that G has a node of degree 0 and a node of degree n−1. (These can't be the same node, since n≥2.) This first node is adjacent to no other nodes, but this second node is adjacent to every other node, which is impossible.

We have reached a contradiction, so our assumption must have been wrong. Thus if G is a graph with at least two nodes, G must have at least two nodes of the same degree. ■

证明二用反证, 不显式引用鸽巢原理: 若度数两两不同, n 个节点占满 n 种度数, 于是 0 和 n − 1 都出现, 同样矛盾. 两个证明的关键都是「0 和 n − 1 不共存」.

推广的鸽巢原理
The Generalized Pigeonhole Principle

Slide 121–130

(动画: 11 个物品放进 5 个盒子, ⌈11/5⌉=3, ⌊11/5⌋=2; 插图 m = 8, n = 3 的鸽子和鸽巢.)

A More General Version

  • The generalized pigeonhole principle says that if you distribute m objects into n bins, then
    • some bin will have at least ⌈m/n⌉ objects in it, and
    • some bin will have at most ⌊m/n⌋ objects in it.

⌈m/n⌉ means “m/n, rounded up.” ⌊m/n⌋ means “m/n, rounded down.”

generalized pigeonhole principle 推广的鸽巢原理: m 个物品放进 n 个盒子, 一定有盒子至少装 ⌈m/n⌉ 个, 也一定有盒子至多装 ⌊m/n⌋ 个. 直觉: 平均每盒 m/n 个, 总有盒子不低于平均, 也总有盒子不高于平均, 而个数是整数, 所以分别取上整和下整.

例子: 11 个放进 5 个盒子, 平均 2.2, 一定有盒子至少 3 个, 也一定有盒子至多 2 个. 8 个放进 3 个盒子, 至少 3 个, 至多 2 个. 原来的鸽巢原理是 m > n 的特例: ⌈m/n⌉≥2.

Slide 131

Theorem: If m objects are distributed into n>0 bins, then some bin will contain at least ⌈m/n⌉ objects.

Proof: We will prove that if m objects are distributed into n bins, then some bin contains at least m/n objects. Since the number of objects in each bin is an integer, this will prove that some bin must contain at least ⌈m/n⌉ objects.

To do this, we proceed by contradiction. Suppose that, for some m and n, there is a way to distribute m objects into n bins such that each bin contains fewer than m/n objects.

Number the bins 1,2,3,…,n and let xi​ denote the number of objects in bin i. Since there are m objects in total, we know that m=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​.

Since each bin contains fewer than m/n objects, we see that xi​<m/n for each i. Therefore, we have that

m​amp;=x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​amp;<m/n+m/n+⋯+m/n(n times)amp;=m.​

But this means that m<m, which is impossible. We have reached a contradiction, so our initial assumption must have been wrong. Therefore, if m objects are distributed into n bins, some bin must contain at least ⌈m/n⌉ objects. ■

证明分两步:

  1. 先证「某个盒子至少 m/n 个」. 反证: 若每个都少于 m/n, 加起来少于 n⋅m/n=m, 得 m < m, 矛盾.
  2. 再从 m/n 推到 ⌈m/n⌉: 盒子里的个数是整数, 一个整数 ≥m/n, 就一定 ≥⌈m/n⌉ (上取整是不小于 m/n 的最小整数).

应用: 朋友与陌生人
An Application: Friends and Strangers

Slide 133–145

Friends and Strangers

  • Suppose you have a party of six people. Each pair of people are either friends (they know each other) or strangers (they do not).
  • Theorem: Any such party must have a group of three mutual friends (three people who all know one another) or three mutual strangers (three people, none of whom know any of the others).

(图: 六个人两两连线, 朋友关系画红线, 陌生关系画蓝线.)

This graph is called a 6-clique, by the way.

Friends and Strangers Restated

  • From a graph-theoretic perspective, the Theorem on Friends and Strangers can be restated as follows:

    Theorem: Any 6-clique whose edges are colored red and blue contains a red triangle or a blue triangle (or both).

  • How can we prove this?

六人派对, 每两人要么是朋友要么是陌生人. 定理: 一定有三个人互为朋友, 或三个人互为陌生人.

图论说法: 六个节点两两相连的图叫 6-clique 6 团 (完全图 K6​). 把每条边涂成红色 (朋友) 或蓝色 (陌生), 一定有一个三条边同色的三角形.

Slide 152

Observation 1: If we pick any node in the graph, that node will have at least ⌈5/2⌉=3 edges of the same color incident to it.

第一个观察: 任取一个节点, 它连着 5 条边, 每条是红或蓝两种颜色之一. 5 个物品放进 2 个盒子, 由推广的鸽巢原理, 有一种颜色至少 ⌈5/2⌉=3 条.

Slide 161

Theorem: Consider a 6-clique in which every edge is colored either red or blue. Then there must be a triangle of red edges, a triangle of blue edges, or both.

Proof: We need to show that the colored 6-clique contains a red triangle or a blue triangle.

Let x be any node in the 6-clique. It is incident to five edges and there are two possible colors for those edges. Therefore, by the generalized pigeonhole principle, at least ⌈5/2⌉=3 of those edges must be the same color. Without loss of generality, assume those edges are blue.

Let r, s, and t be three of the nodes adjacent to node x along a blue edge. If any of the edges {r,s}, {r,t}, or {s,t} are blue, then one of those edges plus the two edges connecting back to node x form a blue triangle. Otherwise, all three of those edges are red, and they form a red triangle. Overall, this gives a red triangle or a blue triangle, as required. ■

证明:

  1. 任取节点 x, 由上面的观察, 它至少有 3 条同色边. 「without loss of generality 不失一般性」假设是蓝色: 红色的情况把颜色互换, 论证完全一样.
  2. 设这 3 条蓝边通向 r、s、t. 看 r、s、t 之间的 3 条边.
  3. 只要其中有一条是蓝的, 比如 {r, s}, 就和 x–r、x–s 组成蓝三角形.
  4. 否则三条全是红的, r、s、t 组成红三角形.

两种情况都有同色三角形. 注意 5 个人的派对不一定成立: 把 5 个人排成一圈, 相邻的是朋友、不相邻的是陌生人, 就既没有三个互为朋友也没有三个互为陌生.

Slide 162

Ramsey Theory

  • The theorem we just proved is a special case of a broader result.
  • Theorem (Ramsey's Theorem): For any natural number n, there is a number R(n) where for any clique with R(n) or more nodes that's painted red or blue, that clique has either a red n-clique or a blue n-clique, and for all cliques with fewer than R(n) nodes, there's a way to paint it red and blue so it has no red n-cliques and no blue n-cliques.
  • Our proof was that R(3)≤6.
  • A more philosophical take on this theorem: true disorder is impossible at a large scale, since no matter how you organize things, you're guaranteed to find some interesting substructure.

这个定理是 Ramsey's theorem 拉姆齐定理的特例: 对任意 n, 存在一个数 R(n), 节点数达到 R(n) 的完全图无论怎样红蓝涂色, 都有一个同色的 n 团; 节点更少时则存在避开它的涂法. 刚才证明了 R(3) ≤ 6, 加上 5 人反例, 实际上 R(3) = 6.

哲学上的解读: 规模足够大时, 完全的无序是不可能的, 总能找到某种规则的子结构. 已知 R(4) = 18, R(5) 至今未知.

Slide 163

Going Further

  • The pigeonhole principle can be used to prove a ton of amazing theorems. Here's a sampler:
    • There is always a way to fairly split rent among multiple people, even if different people want different rooms. (Sperner's lemma)
    • You and a friend can climb any mountain from two different starting points so that the two of you maintain the same altitude at each point in time. (Mountain-climbing theorem)
    • If you model coffee in a cup as a collection of infinitely many points and then stir the coffee, some point is always where it initially started. (Brower's fixed-point theorem)
    • A complex process that doesn't parallelize well must contain a large serial subprocess. (Mirksy's theorem)
    • Any positive integer n has a nonzero multiple that can be written purely using the digits 1 and 0. (Doesn't have a name, but still cool!)

延伸: 鸽巢原理 (及其连续版本) 能证明很多结论, 如房租公平分配 (Sperner 引理)、登山定理、布劳威尔不动点定理 (搅咖啡后总有一点回到原位)、Mirsky 定理, 以及「每个正整数都有一个只由 0 和 1 写成的非零倍数」.

最后一条可以自己试: 看 1, 11, 111, …, 共 n + 1 个数除以 n 的余数, 余数只有 n 种, 由鸽巢原理有两个余数相同, 它们的差 (形如 11…100…0) 是 n 的倍数.

原文笔误: “Brower's fixed-point theorem” 应为 Brouwer's (荷兰数学家 L. E. J. Brouwer); “Mirksy's theorem” 应为 Mirsky's (Leon Mirsky).
